digest.top_line: APCCC 2026: consensus (≥75%) on 44 of 134 high-risk/locally advanced PC questions (32.8%); fractionation for high-risk localised PC reached none despite 88% favoring some hypofractionation.
digest.tldr: APCCC 2026 panel opinion on high-risk localised PC: RT + long-term ADT ± ARPI is the plurality pick, while fractionation stays unsettled.

studies.name: APCCC 2026: High-risk Localised, Locally Advanced, and Biochemically Recurrent PC
studies.tldr: Consensus (≥75%) reached on 44 of 134 questions (32.8%); fractionation for high-risk localised PC reached no consensus despite 88% favoring some hypofractionation.

🔗 ENZARAD lower risk than STAMPEDE: cN1 11% vs 39%, cT3–T4 47% vs 94%
🔗 DIL focal boost RCT (>500 pts): 77 Gy/35 fx whole gland ± boost up to 95 Gy → better bPFS, lower local failure
🔗 SHARP pooled SBRT (440 high-risk pts): 5-yr BCR 22%, DM 9.2%, G2 GU 23%, G2 GI 10%
⚠️ HYPO-RT-PC only 11% high-risk; ultrahypofractionation evidence for high-risk is scarce per authors

⚠️ Votes are opinion; authors state no formal literature review or meta-analysis
studies.significance: Fractionation drew 88% for some form of hypofractionation but no consensus on which form, and 44 panellists abstained or declared themselves unqualified. Moderate hypofractionation (2.5–3.4 Gy/fx) is framed as the established option. SBRT for high-risk disease rests on non-randomised SHARP pooling, with 5-yr G2 GU toxicity of 23%, so it stays a trial question.
studies.monday_clinic: In very high-risk cN0 PC planned for RT + long-term ADT, panel opinion (65–71%) favors adding 2 yr abiraterone over enzalutamide. This does not settle the choice between ultrahypofractionation and moderate hypofractionation for high-risk disease.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Modified Delphi process: **144 international experts** drafted 313 multiple-choice questions, 134 on high-risk localised / locally advanced PC, PSA persistence and recurrence. **133 panellists** voted by web survey before the conference.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: Consensus defined a priori as **75% agreement**, strong consensus **90%**. Consensus reached on **44 of 134 questions (32.8%)**, seven of them strong.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **No consensus on fractionation** (Q19) despite a combined 88% favoring some hypofractionation. Moderate hypofractionation (2.5–3.4 Gy per fraction) is named as an option. MRI-defined DIL focal boost up to 95 Gy over 77 Gy in 35 fractions is described as validated in a randomised trial.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: Very high-risk disease: RT + long-term ADT (2–3 yr) with the option of **abiraterone for 2 yr**. A combined 83% voted ADT can be stopped after 2 yr with abiraterone in most or selected pts (Q7).

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: The intensification votes follow STAMPEDE over ENZARAD, whose null MFS (**HR 0.88**, 95% CI 0.67–1.15) came in a lower-risk population. ATLAS, PEACE-7, THUNDER and DASL-HiCaP are testing other ARPIs in this setting.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents high-risk and very high-risk localised and locally advanced PC staged cN0 M0 on conventional or next-generation imaging. Does not represent metastatic hormone-sensitive or castration-resistant disease.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: 44 panellists abstained or declared themselves unqualified on fractionation, which shrinks the informed denominator. The Q6 vote against perioperative ADT + ARPI before RP **predates PROTEUS**, which was presented and published after the conference.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The panel accepts RT and multimodal surgery as defensible for high-risk cN0 disease without settling the comparison. Its abiraterone-not-enzalutamide vote is drug-specific, not a class effect, and the ongoing ARPI trials will decide whether that distinction holds.

studies.interpretation:
For a radiation oncologist, this report is most useful where the panel split, not where it agreed. Only 44 of 134 questions crossed the prespecified 75% threshold. The questions closest to daily RT practice, treatment selection for high-risk cN0 disease and fractionation, both fell short of it. The 62–68% vote for RT plus long-term ADT ± ARPI over a multimodal surgical approach describes a field that treats both pathways as defensible, not one that has resolved the comparison. None of the evidence the authors cite tests RT against surgery directly in this population.

The intensification votes follow the trial evidence closely. A panel majority backs 2 yr abiraterone in very high-risk disease, and very few panellists voted for enzalutamide. That mirrors the split between STAMPEDE and ENZARAD. The authors point out that ENZARAD enrolled a lower-risk population (cN1 11% vs 39%, cT3–T4 47% vs 94%). Its null MFS result (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.67–1.15) therefore does not cleanly test ARPI substitution in the population STAMPEDE treated. The panel is voting on drug-specific evidence, not a class effect, and that is defensible. ATLAS, PEACE-7, THUNDER and DASL-HiCaP will show whether the distinction holds, especially in pts without pelvic nodal disease. The ENZARAD signal in cN1 disease, or when pelvic RT is given for another reason, is preplanned but still a subgroup. It should not yet move practice on its own.

Fractionation is where a quick read of the vote misleads most. A combined 88% for some form of hypofractionation sounds decisive. But no single schedule reached consensus, and 44 panellists abstained or called themselves unqualified, so informed opinion is a smaller group than the headline suggests. The cited evidence supports caution on ultrahypofractionation for high-risk disease. HYPO-RT-PC had few high-risk pts, and the SHARP data are pooled from non-randomised prospective series. Moderate hypofractionation is presented as the established option. SBRT for high-risk localised disease remains a question for trials.

The focal boost discussion is the most transferable RT content. The authors describe a randomised trial in which an MRI-defined boost of up to 95 Gy on top of 77 Gy in 35 fractions improved bPFS and local failure, with no significant difference in late GU or GI toxicity. This makes dose escalation to the dominant lesion an option alongside conventional fractionation. How boost combines with moderate hypofractionation or SBRT is not addressed in the material provided.

The document generates no new outcome data. The authors say there was no formal literature review or meta-analysis, and the votes are distributions of expert opinion. One timing problem deserves attention. The consensus against perioperative ADT + ARPI before RP was reached before PROTEUS was presented and published. That trial reported a higher pCR or minimal residual disease rate and an MFS difference driven by PSMA-PET. So the Q6 vote reflects pre-PROTEUS opinion and may move when the question returns at the 2027 localised consensus conference.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Fractionation reached no consensus: 88% favored some hypofractionation, and 44 panellists abstained. Moderate hypofractionation (2.5–3.4 Gy/fx) is the established option, while SBRT for high-risk disease rests on non-randomised SHARP pooling. DIL focal boost up to 95 Gy over 77 Gy/35 fx is presented as validated dose escalation.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: In very high-risk cN0 disease, 65–71% backed 2 yr abiraterone with RT + long-term ADT, and very few backed enzalutamide, tracking ENZARAD's null MFS (HR 0.88). A combined 83% would stop ADT after 2 yr with abiraterone. ATLAS, PEACE-7, THUNDER and DASL-HiCaP will test other ARPIs.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: 32–38% favored surgery as part of a multimodal approach for high-risk cN0 disease. The panel reached consensus against perioperative ADT + ARPI before RP, but voted before PROTEUS (pCR/MRD 8.9% vs 1.0%) was presented, so that position may shift.

papers.title: Management of Patients with High-risk Localised, Locally Advanced, and Biochemically Recurrent Prostate Cancer: Report from the 2026 Advanced Prostate Cancer Consensus Conference
RADIANT: A radiotherapy foundation model for treatment planning and outcome prediction across cancers
papers.abstract:
ESMO Congress 2026 abstract 170O · Proffered paper: AI and digital health · 2026-10-24 · presented by Zhen Zhang (Hangzhou, China)

Background: Radiotherapy generates structured planning CT, target/OAR contours and 3D dose maps, yet current AI tools are usually single-task models trained in limited cohorts. We developed RADIANT, a radiotherapy foundation model for an automated workflow from target delineation and dose generation to clinical risk prediction.
Methods: RADIANT used a 3D Swin Transformer encoder pretrained by masked autoencoding on 119,782 radiotherapy cases from 14 centres with paired planning CT, RT structure sets and 3D dose distributions. The encoder was refined with hierarchical GTV/CTV segmentation and dose generation. Outputs were tested in a hold-out set of 22,058 cases from the 10 most prevalent tumour sites. For downstream adaptation, a frozen RADIANT encoder was integrated with a generated-dose branch and task-specific heads for 21 endpoints across lung, oesophageal, rectal and cervical cancers. Validation included retrospective and prospective cohorts from China, the United States and the Netherlands, covering pCR/response, OS, PFS, LC and radiotherapy-related toxicities. Performance was compared with state-of-the-art baseline models.
Results: In hold-out testing, RADIANT achieved overall Dice scores of 83.52% for GTV and 81.53% for CTV, with dose-generation errors of 0.0695 for ΔHI, 0.0706 for ΔD98, 0.0129 for ΔD2, 0.0012 for ΔDmax and 0.0371 for ΔDmean. Across independent validations, RADIANT achieved AUCs of 0.72 for pCR after oesophageal nICT, 0.84 for rectal complete response, 0.78-0.81 for radiation pneumonitis, 0.84-0.85 for rectal radiation proctitis and 0.84 for cervical radiation proctitis. Survival models yielded external C-indices of 0.73-0.79 for OS, 0.71-0.78 for PFS and 0.76-0.86 for LC/LRC. RADIANT consistently outperformed baseline models, particularly in external cohorts. Grad-CAM highlighted clinically plausible tumour and normal-tissue dose interfaces; exploratory transcriptomic analyses suggested biological differences between model-defined risk groups.
Conclusions: Prospective and international multi-centre validation supports RADIANT as a scalable framework for AI-assisted radiotherapy workflows and decision-making.

papers.title: A phase II trial of neoadjuvant nivolumab, docetaxel, and cisplatin followed by surgery and radiation therapy for resectable high-grade salivary gland carcinoma
papers.abstract:
ESMO Congress 2026 abstract 1540RO · Rapid oral: Head and neck cancer · 2026-10-25 · presented by Sehhoon Park (Seoul, Republic of Korea) · NCT05727410

Background: Resectable high-grade salivary gland carcinoma (SGC) with clinical node metastasis carries a high risk of distant metastasis despite curative surgery and adjuvant radiotherapy, and effective neoadjuvant strategies remain undefined. We evaluated neoadjuvant nivolumab plus docetaxel and cisplatin (NivoDP) in this aggressive disease.
Methods: This phase II, single-center, single-arm trial enrolled treatment-naïve patients with resectable high-grade SGC and clinically positive lymph nodes. Patients received 3 cycles of nivolumab (360 mg) plus docetaxel (60 mg/m2) and cisplatin (60 mg/m2) q3w, followed by curative surgery and risk-adapted adjuvant radiotherapy. The primary endpoint was major pathologic response (MPR; ≤10% viable tumor).
Results: Of 55 enrolled, 4 screen failures and 1 with benign histology were excluded, leaving 50 analyzed (median age 62; 88.0% male; ECOG 0/1: 12.0%/88.0%). AJCC 8th stage was III/IVA/IVB in 34.0%/64.0%/2.0%. Salivary duct carcinoma predominated (74.0%), followed by adenocarcinoma (10.0%) and mucoepidermoid carcinoma (8.0%). ORR was 52.0%. Forty-six patients underwent surgery (92.0%); 4 did not (1 withdrawal, 2 progression, 1 G3 drug-induced pneumonitis). Among 46 operated patients, R0 resection was 93.5%, MPR 60.9% (n=28), and pCR 32.6% (n=15), exceeding the predefined threshold (MPR ≥50%). Among pathology subtypes, salivary duct carcinoma (MPR 67.6%, pCR 29.4%), adenocarcinoma (MPR 75.0%, pCR 75.0%), and poorly differentiated carcinoma (MPR 66.7%, pCR 66.7%) showed the best response to NivoDP. With a median follow-up of 16.2 months (95% CI 12.0–20.1) from surgery, 12- and 24-month DFS were 89.0% and 76.0%, and 24-month OS 91.2%. The MPR subgroup showed significantly longer DFS than non-MPR (NR vs 24.2 mo; HR 0.19, 95% CI 0.05–0.71, p=0.013). Most TRAEs were grade 1–2; 6 grade ≥3 TRAEs were observed, which were all manageable with no treatment-related deaths.
Conclusions: Neoadjuvant NivoDP showed promising clinical efficacy in node-positive high-grade SGC, with high MPR and pCR rates. MPR strongly predicted superior DFS. These results support neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy as a promising strategy in resectable high-grade SGC.
Clinical trial identification: NCT05727410.

papers.title: First interim safety analysis of GORTEC 2024-03 IDEAL: Randomized phase II trial of induction treatment anti–PD-1 pucotenlimab (HX008) plus EGFR-ADC (becotatug vedotin (MRG003) versus EGFR-ADC alone followed by chemoradiotherapy in locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
papers.abstract:
ESMO Congress 2026 abstract 1538RO · Rapid oral: Head and neck cancer · 2026-10-25 · presented by Yungan Tao (Villejuif, France) · NCT06959108

Background: The EGFR-directed ADC becotatug vedotin (MRG003) alone or combined with anti-PD1 pucotenlimab (HX008) have shown promising efficacy along with a good safety profile in R/M HNSCC (Xue, Clin. Cancer Res. 2026). The IDEAL trial evaluates induction becotatug vedotin ± pucotenlimab prior to definitive chemoradiotherapy (CRT) in locally advanced (LA) HNSCC.
Methods: Patients (pts) with LA-HNSCC (larynx, hypopharynx, oral cavity, and oropharynx [p16 - and p16 +]) were randomized (1:1) to 2 arms: (A) induction pucotenlimab (200 mg) + becotatug vedotin (2.3 mg/kg) Q3W ×3 → CRT → adjuvant pucotenlimab (Q3W ×8), or (B) induction ADC alone → CRT. CRT consisted of IMRT (70 Gy) + concurrent cisplatin. Primary endpoint is complete response (CR) at 12 weeks post-CRT. Each arm is evaluated independently (one-stage Fleming design; H0=30%). A total of 106 pts is planned. The first interim safety analysis was conducted after completion of cycle 1 in first 20 pts.
Results: Between October 23rd 2025 and April 21st 2026, 49 pts were randomized. Most had oropharyngeal cancer (31 pts, including 19 p16 +). 20 patients (10 per arm) were evaluated for first safety analysis. One death occurred in Arm B (post-gastrostomy, after 1 cycle ADC), deemed unrelated to study treatment. No grade 4 adverse events (AEs) were observed in either arm. A total of 11 Grade 3 TEAEs were observed in 8 pts (6 arm A and 2 arm B). In arm A, these G3 TEAEs were ALT increase + constipation (1 pt), myalgia + ALT increase + hypertension (1), neutropenia (1), diabetes (1), diarrhea (1) and hyponatremia (1). In Arm B, G3 TEAEs were peripheral arterial ischemia (1) and fatigue (1). Data on ORR (per RECIST 1.1) after induction are preliminary and not mature, but ORR observed in 71% of first 15 evaluable pts. Updated safety and post-induction ORR data will be presented at the meeting along with preliminary results on primary endpoint.
Conclusions: First results of induction becotatug vedotin ± pucotenlimab in LA-SCCHN are encouraging and a favorable safety profile was observed.
Clinical trial identification: NCT06959108 First Submitted: 2025-04-28, EU CT 2023-510558-18-00.

papers.title: A single-arm, multi-institutional, phase 2 study of a pembrolizumab-based organ preservation strategy for locally advanced larynx cancers: SMART-KEY (LACOG 0720)
papers.abstract:
ESMO Congress 2026 abstract 1537RO · Rapid oral: Head and neck cancer · 2026-10-25 · presented by Thiago B. Oliveira (Sao Paulo, Brazil) · NCT04943445

Background: Standard larynx-preserving strategies yield similar laryngectomy-free survival (LFS) with no overall survival (OS) difference, but data raise concerns about late-onset toxicity and mortality, especially for concurrent cisplatin/radiation therapy (RT). We evaluated the addition of pembrolizumab to a cisplatin-free induction, concurrent and consolidation strategy for larynx-preservation.
Methods: This multicenter, single-arm phase 2 trial enrolled patients (pts) with newly diagnosed stage III–IVB glottic/supraglottic squamous cell carcinomas. Pts received induction carboplatin AUC6, paclitaxel 175 mg/m2, and pembrolizumab 200 mg (three 21-day cycles), followed by IMRT with pembrolizumab alone and fourteen 21-day cycles of pembrolizumab consolidation. Primary endpoint was two-year (2y) LFS.
Results: From Feb 2022 to Aug 2023, 43 pts from 9 centers were enrolled (median age 61.1y, 86% male, 74.4% White, 25.6% Black/Mixed, 83.7% former/current smokers, 62.8% glottic). The 2y LFS was 65.1% (80% CI: 54.9-73.5), which compares favorably with historical pivotal trials results. Additional outcomes are presented in the Table. Two-year cumulative incidence of locoregional and distant recurrence were 18.8% and 7.4%. Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events occurred in 41.9% pts (one pt with grade 5), with immune-mediated grade ≥3 TRAEs in 16.3%. Table: 1537RO Outcomes SMART-KEY Historical Control RTOG 9111 (Cisplatin+RT) Historical Control GORTEC 2000-01 (cisplatin, docetaxel, 5-fluorouracil/RT) 2y laryngectomy-free survival 65.1% 64.9% NE 2y larynx preservation rates 86% 88% 75.8% 2y larynx dysfunction-free survival 83.7% NE 70.3% 2y overall survival 74.4% 74% 73% Proportion of pts Alive with larynx 65.1% 64.9% NE Alive after laryngectomy 9.3% 9.1% NE Dead after laryngectomy 4.7% 2.9% NE Dead no laryngectomy 20.9% 23.1% NE
Conclusions: SMART-KEY demonstrated short-term oncological/functional outcomes numerically comparable to RTOG-9111 and potentially superior to GORTEC 2000-01, pivotal trials using cisplatin-based regimens. Our well-tolerated cisplatin-free, concurrent chemotherapy-free strategy also yielded low rates of distant recurrence. The long-term benefit of this regimen will be evaluated with additional follow-up but may have the potential to mitigate cisplatin/RT-related late morbidity/mortality.
Clinical trial identification: NCT04943445.

papers.title: ctDNA analysis of the phase 3 KEYNOTE-412 trial: Pembrolizumab (pembro) or placebo (pbo) + concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CRT) for locally advanced head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (LA HNSCC)
papers.abstract:
ESMO Congress 2026 abstract 1536RO · Rapid oral: Head and neck cancer · 2026-10-25 · presented by Jean-Pascal Machiels (Woluwe-Saint-Lambert, Belgium) · NCT03040999

Background: ctDNA is an emerging biomarker in multiple solid tumor types, but its value in LA HNSCC is unclear. KEYNOTE-412 (NCT03040999) evaluated pembro + CRT vs pbo + CRT in participants (pts) with newly diagnosed, unresected LA HNSCC. We retrospectively assessed the association of clinical outcomes with pretreatment ctDNA (baseline [BL] ctDNA) and early on-treatment ctDNA (cycle 3 day 1 [C3D1] ctDNA in pts who completed 5 of 6-7 wk of CRT) in KEYNOTE-412.
Methods: The tumor-informed Natera Signatera 16-plex assay was used to evaluate ctDNA levels in treated pts. Association of BL ctDNA levels and C3D1 ctDNA clearance with EFS and OS were assessed in each arm and by HPV status (by p16 testing) per Cox proportional hazards regression.
Results: Of 804 pts, 473 (pembro arm n = 233; pbo arm n = 240) had evaluable ctDNA samples at both BL and C3D1. BL ctDNA positivity rate was 95.6% for HPV+ and 95.3% for HPV- pts. BL ctDNA levels were positively correlated with BL target lesion size in both HPV- and HPV+ pts (Spearman ρ = 0.49 and 0.34, respectively). Higher BL ctDNA levels were associated with worse OS in the pembro arm and worse EFS and OS in the pbo arm in HPV- pts (P < 0.05); no associations in either arm were observed in HPV+ pts (P > 0.05). The association of BL ctDNA levels with outcomes in HPV- pts was independent of ECOG PS but dependent on tumor size and stage. ctDNA clearance rate at C3D1 was higher in the pembro arm (HPV- 72.6%; HPV+ 76.8%) vs pbo arm (HPV- 63.6%; HPV+ 62.7%). In HPV- pts, ctDNA clearance at C3D1 was associated with improved EFS in both arms (pembro P = 0.001; pbo P = 0.011) and with improved OS in the pembro arm (P < 0.001) but not in the pbo arm (P = 0.075). In HPV+ pts, ctDNA clearance at C3D1 was associated with improved EFS (P = 0.028) and OS (P = 0.013) only in the pbo arm.
Conclusions: The prognostic value of BL ctDNA was observed in HPV- pts with LA HNSCC but not in HPV+ pts. In HPV- pts, a stronger link between C3D1 ctDNA clearance and long-term survival was observed in the pembro arm. These findings suggest distinct ctDNA prognostic values in HNSCC based on HPV status, and long-term outcome associations may differ by treatment modality.
Clinical trial identification: NCT03040999.
